newsitem.title: NORWAY: POLL - Update Norwegian election surveys.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Update Norwegian election surveys.

text.p: Two opinion polls released on Friday, one month before the Norwegian election, showed the ruling Labour (LP) minority government losing support while the far-right Progress Party (PP) made heavy gains compared with the 1993 election.
Projected percentage for each party (figures are rounded)
LP PP C CPP CP V SL RE others
NOTE -- The MMI poll was carried out on August 11-13 and questioned a sample of 966 voters. The OPI poll was carried out during the same time period and included 1,001 voters.
LP PP H CPP CP V SL RE others

NOTE -- Labour Party (LP), Progress Party (PP), Conservatives (C), Christian People's Party (CPP), Centre Party (CP), Liberal Venstre (V), Socialist Left Party (SL) Red Election Alliance (RE). Norwegians elect a new 165-seat parliament on September 15. The Labour Party, which has been in power since 1990, tends to rule alone finding support on a case-by-case basis from several parties in parliament. The three centrist parties -- the Centre Party, the Christian People's Party and the liberal Venstre -- want to form a coalition government.
